meta.seasons_note: Seasons are labelled by harvest year. Crops whose season crosses New Year (e.g. potato Nov–Mar) have 44 complete seasons (1981/82–2024/25); calendar-year and Jan-sown crops have 45 (1981–2025). 2025/26 is incomplete and is not counted. No season is padded.
meta.base_series: NASA POWER daily (community AG) only: PRECTOTCORR, T2M_MIN/T2M_MAX, ET0 FAO-56 PM from POWER (pipeline et0_pm), GWETROOT (reported, not used for failures)

base_series_handling.precip_qc: pipeline rule: drop POWER days >50 mm whose CHIRPS v3 month total <25% of that day (removed 2022-09-12/13)

temperature.carumas: POWER + 4.55 °C lapse shift (6.5 °C/km, 3,851 m cell → 3,151 m SRTM), as pipeline
temperature.samegua: POWER + 14.79 °C lapse shift (same cell, → 1,575 m). Pipeline risk_build prefers ERA5-Land for Samegua frost; with a POWER-only base we keep the lapse-adjusted series and report ERA5-Land as validation (both give 0 frost days)

base_series_handling.et0: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith on raw POWER (pipeline convention for crop water). 1981–1983 lack POWER radiation: POWER Hargreaves (FAO-56 eq. 52) calibrated to POWER PM by calendar-month ratio 1984–2010

validation_overlays: ERA5 daily precipitation (0.25°) and ERA5-Land Tmin/Tmax (0.1°) via Open-Meteo archive API (ERA5-Land precipitation is null at these points, so ERA5 is used for rain)
GPM IMERG Final Run monthly v07 (GPM_3IMERGM) via GES DISC OPeNDAP, 1998-01..2025-09
SMAP L3 SPL3SMP_E v006 9 km AM soil moisture, Carumas cell, 2015-04..

method.water: Daily FAO-56 single-layer root-zone water balance (ch. 8) per crop season, ETc = ET0 × Kc (FAO-56 Table 12), Zr and p from FAO-56 Table 22 (lower bound of Zr range), TAW 120 mm/m (FAO-56 Table 19, sandy loam midpoints; SoilGrids texture = sandy loam at all farms). Seasonal WRSI = 100 × ΣETa/ΣETc (Frère & Popov 1979, FAO PPP 17). Failure: WRSI < 50; stress: WRSI < 80 (Smith 1992 / FEWS NET categories). Carumas uses the WRSI anomaly (% of the crop's 1991–2020 median), as recommended for arid zones.
method.irrigation: Irrigated farms: water failure = modelled supply vs crop demand, not rain. Normal-year allotment = current practice's 1991–2020 monthly gross need (ET0×Kc − effective rain)/0.60 (alfalfa at Samegua, olive at El Algarrobal). Each year it is scaled by a supply index S = min(1, Jan–Mar POWER rain at the 3,851 m upper-basin cell / its 1991–2020 median); Samegua averages S over 2 years (Pasto Grande reservoir), El Algarrobal uses 1 year (Osmore, run-of-river). Every strategy receives the same allotment; efficiencies gravity 0.60, sprinkler 0.75, drip 0.90 (Brouwer et al. 1989). Olive RDI 0.75, cover Kc 0.8 on 50% (cover) / 30% strips (drip) May–Sep, as in the pipeline. ASSUMPTION: the supply proxy is not a measured canal/turno record.
method.frost: Frost failure: any day with Tmin ≤ the cold end of the FLOWERING critical-temperature range during the crop's peak-Kc months, or ≤ the GERMINATION value in the sowing month (FAO 2005 Frost Protection Vol. 1, Table 4.5, after Ventskevich 1958). Frost damage (reported): Tmin ≤ warm end of the flowering range.
method.heat: Not a failure cause (no cited crop-stage threshold retrieved and lapse-adjusted Samegua Tmax runs warm vs ERA5-Land); heat days >30 °C at flowering are kept in the raw hindcast only.
method.rotations: Every phase every year: each crop of a rotation is hindcast in every season (standard rotation-trial design). Season fails if any cropped phase fails; fallow phases cannot fail. fail_share = failed phases / cropped phases.
method.enso: ONI v5 (NOAA CPC oni.ascii.txt), DJF value of the wet season that drives the crop season (DJF of the harvest year for Nov–Mar crops; DJF Dec(y-1)–Feb(y) for calendar-year crops). El Niño ≥ +0.5, La Niña ≤ −0.5, else neutral.
method.tests: Fisher's exact test (El Niño vs other, seasons with ≥1 failure), 3-phase permutation test (20,000 shuffles of ENSO labels; statistic = range of failure rates), Mann-Whitney U on season WRSI (El Niño vs other) and Kruskal-Wallis across 3 phases. n per phase is reported; with ~15 seasons per phase and 0–3 failures the failure tests have low power.

meta.imerg_access: WORKS (tested 2026-11-14 with EARTHDATA_TOKEN via GES DISC OPeNDAP): GPM_3IMERGM v07 Final monthly, 333 months 1998-01..2025-09 pulled for all 3 farm cells, 0 failures (data/raw/imerg_monthly_final_v07.csv). Final Run ends 2025-09 in CMR; no 1981-2025 season needs IMERG Late. Used only as a validation overlay.
gaps: Model-based hindcast: no observed plot yields, canal/turno deliveries or reservoir records were available; irrigation supply is a rainfall-based proxy (assumption).
Crop calendars, rotation phases and Kc for quinoa/tarwi/oat-vetch are assumptions (not INIA-confirmed). No INIA Moquegua crop-threshold table was retrievable; FAO thresholds used.

POWER rain at the 3,851 m cell is dry-biased (Nov–Mar 1991–2020 mean 101.5 mm vs CHIRPS 205 mm; 2001–2025 IMERG 273 mm vs POWER 100 mm), so Carumas uses WRSI anomalies; absolute WRSI fails in 44/44 potato seasons with POWER rain and 10/24 with IMERG rain.

Frost: 0.5° grid Tmin cannot resolve cold-air pooling on terraces/valley floors; the lapse-adjusted POWER series has an absolute minimum of -0.2 °C at Carumas (ERA5-Land -6.8 °C), so in-season frost failures may be under-counted.
Samegua and Carumas share one POWER cell; Samegua lapse-adjusted Tmax runs ~7 °C warmer than ERA5-Land, so heat is not used as a failure cause.
SMAP is available for the Carumas cell only (9 km, 2015+); 10 complete seasons.
ERA5-Land precipitation is null at these points via Open-Meteo, so ERA5 (0.25°) rain is used for the cross-check; ERA5 is ~7x wetter than POWER at Carumas.
ENSO failure tests have low power: ~13-16 seasons per phase and 0-3 failures per strategy.
1981-1983 ET0 uses calibrated POWER Hargreaves (no POWER radiation before 1984).

named_years.title: 2023–24 El Niño (ONI DJF 2023/24 = 1.84)
named_years.season_mapping: Carumas season 2023/24 (Nov 2023–Mar 2024); irrigated farms: calendar 2024, whose supply index uses Jan–Mar 2024 upper-basin rain. Note: DJF 2022/23 (start of the 2023 coastal El Niño) was still La Niña by ONI.
named_years.text: Model-based hindcast, not observed yields. Carumas: POWER Nov 2023–Mar 2024 rain was near its normal (potato WRSI 101.4% of its 1991–2020 median), so no rotation shows a water or frost failure. Irrigated valleys: the supply proxy fell to 0.58 (Samegua, 2-season memory) and 0.69 (El Algarrobal) of normal. Samegua: continuous alfalfa (today) falls to WRSI 67.3 (mediocre) vs 78.0 (mediocre) for CERES's alfalfa → forage maize → pea. El Algarrobal: gravity irrigation on bare soil reaches WRSI 82.0 (average) vs 100.0 (very good) for CERES's drip + strip cover, with the same canal allotment. No strategy fails outright in 2024; the recommended strategies keep more of the crop's water demand satisfied.

named_years.title: 1982–83 El Niño (ONI DJF 1982/83 = 2.14): the worst season in the record
named_years.text: Model-based hindcast. Nov 1982–Mar 1983 POWER rain at the highland cell was the lowest of the record; potato WRSI fell to 38.8% of normal (water failure) and every Carumas rotation failed on water. The El Algarrobal supply proxy fell to 0.10 of normal: every olive strategy fails (current WRSI 23.4, drip 26.7). Some droughts are beyond any rotation; CERES's role there is early warning and water-saving that stretches the reservoir, not a guarantee.

named_years.title: 2015–16 El Niño (ONI DJF 2015/16 = 2.5) and the 2016 El Algarrobal olive losses
named_years.reality_check: ProActivo (01/12/2016): Moquegua's regional agriculture manager reported S/ 21 M of losses and that in El Algarrobal 'se perdió más del 50 % de plantaciones de olivo' (press report, not a measured yield series).
named_years.text: Model-based hindcast. The 2016 supply proxy at El Algarrobal was 0.72 of normal. Gravity/bare soil drops to WRSI 80.0 (edge of the stress band), cover 72.3, drip + strip cover 98.5. The hindcast flags stress, not outright failure, so it UNDER-calls the reported >50% olive losses; the late-2016 dry spell (Sep–Dec) falls outside the Jan–Mar supply window used here. We report this as a limitation.
